answer: Each identity runs one ridge relay and locks a 90-credit bond. Its crystal meter signs a traffic count, and any auditor can recompute the total from signed counts. A relay earns if its count matches within 5 percent; a mismatch burns the bond. Each slot is one yarrow plot, and the board rejects a second claim on it. The k-th registration costs 30 plus 4 times the earlier count, so the 1000th costs 4026; 1000 fakes pay 2028000 in fees plus 90000 locked. A rented-meter ring fails: one crystal signature cannot cover two slots. An honest operator pays 90 plus 30 once.
